title: Meghna Gulzar Says Daayra Reveals an 'Entirely Unseen' Kareena Kapoor Khan
excerpt: Director praises Kareena's stoic, unreadable performance as crime thriller's trailer approaches August 31 launch
body:
• Director Meghna Gulzar calls Kareena Kapoor Khan's performance in Daayra an "entirely unseen facet" of the actor, describing her character as "stoic, unreadable" ahead of the trailer launch on August 31
  • Daayra, a crime thriller inspired by true events, marks the first on-screen pairing of Kareena and Malayalam star Prithviraj Sukumaran, who play law enforcement officers on opposing sides of a moral divide
  • The film releases September 18, reuniting Gulzar with Junglee Pictures for the third time after Talvar and Raazi, with Pen Studios co-producing

Director Meghna Gulzar has described Kareena Kapoor Khan's performance in her upcoming crime thriller Daayra as revealing an "entirely unseen facet" of the actor, raising anticipation ahead of the film's trailer launch on August 31.

In an Instagram note shared this week, Gulzar wrote: "Daayra unveils an entirely unseen facet of the actor that is Kareena Kapoor. Kareena as Ajooni, is stoic, unreadable. She cracks open situations and people with a smile."

Two Actors, Two Industries, One Story

Daayra (meaning "Circle") pairs Kareena with Malayalam cinema star Prithviraj Sukumaran in their first on-screen collaboration. Both play officers of law enforcement — Kareena as ACP Ajooni Kohli and Prithviraj as Raman Kumar — but their contrasting approaches to justice and morality form the film's central tension.

"Prithviraj Sukumaran as Raman, is the hinge to Kareena's Ajooni. Seething with a caged rage. And almost never smiles. The two are the Ying and Yang of Daayra. And that's just one of the many dualities that Daayra navigates."

— Meghna Gulzar, Director

Gulzar described the casting as "a dream come true," calling it a rare opportunity to bring together two prominent actors from the Hindi and Malayalam film industries. The film marks Kareena's first collaboration with a director known for restrained, investigative storytelling, a departure from the star's typical commercial filmography.

Inspired by True Events

Unlike Gulzar's previous films Talvar (2015) and Raazi (2018), which drew from specific real-life incidents, Daayra draws from multiple true events across India rather than a single case. The filmmaker has said the story explores "duality" — in characters, in the justice system, and in public perception.

"Society is not binary," Gulzar told Cinema Express. "At its core, Daayra is only about duality. And this duality is entrenched through the two main protagonists of the film."

She described Ajooni as "fiercely righteous" and Raman as "righteously fierce," noting that both characters operate in moral grey areas where the law serves as both guide and constraint.

Production and Creative Team

Daayra is produced by Junglee Pictures and Dr. Jayantilal Gada's Pen Studios, marking the first collaboration between the two production houses. For Gulzar, it represents her third partnership with Junglee Pictures, continuing a creative relationship that has produced two of Bollywood's most acclaimed thrillers.

The film is written by Gulzar alongside Yash Keswani and Sima Agarwal. Principal photography began in late September 2025 and wrapped in December 2025. Notably, the film contains no songs — Gulzar's father, the legendary poet Gulzar, confirmed the decision, saying "Meghna thought adding songs would break up the story's flow."

The supporting cast includes Prithviraj Sukumaran, Pragati Mishra, Javed Khan King, and Upendra Chauhan.

What It Means for Bollywood

Kareena's choice of Daayra signals a deliberate pivot toward performance-driven roles in her career's third decade. In her Instagram response, Kareena wrote: "There are films you do, and then there are films that make you sit with things you may not always want to think about. Daayra and becoming ACP Ajooni Kohli, did that for me."

For the Indian diaspora audience, the pairing of a Hindi and Malayalam industry star in a song-less crime thriller reflects Bollywood's evolving appetite for cross-industry collaborations and content-driven cinema — a trend accelerated by the pan-Indian success of films like RRR and KGF.

Daayra is scheduled for theatrical release on September 18, 2026, distributed by Pen Marudhar.
